name: editor_docs
description: Every text of the electrical editor page: the Documentation sections (text), the hover popups (tips: at most 4 bullets of about 12 words, keywords in **bold**), the status messages, How to use and What's new. One home: vpt/editor_page.py and the page script read them from here; vpt/docs.py checks the popup length when the page is built.
title: Elektroplan Editor
intro: Plan where the electrical outlets, switches and lights of a flat go, on top of the architect's drawing. The drawing is a plan file exported from a DXF on your own computer (tools/export_plan.py); this page reads it in your browser and never sends it anywhere.

banners.synthetic_more: The drawing is the toolkit's invented sample flat (samples/synthetic_flat.dxf). Open your own plan file to work on your drawing.
banners.own_plan: Plan file: {file} (read in this browser only; nothing is uploaded).
banners.artifact_note: This is the shareable demo. To save files or print, use the GitHub Pages version: {url} (it works once the repository is public). Here: copy the layout or the parameters, and the draft stays in this browser.
banners.pages_note: Files you open are read in this browser only; Save writes to your computer. Nothing is uploaded.

in.label: Zoom in (+)
in.text: Zooms in on the centre of the drawing. To zoom around the pointer instead: pinch on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) and turn the mouse wheel.

out.label: Zoom out (−)
out.text: Zooms out from the centre of the drawing. To zoom around the pointer instead: pinch on a trackpad, or hold Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) and turn the mouse wheel.

pan.label: Pan (drag) and zoom (pinch, Ctrl/⌘ + wheel)
pan.text: Drag the empty drawing with the mouse (or a finger) to move it. Pinch, or Ctrl (⌘ on a Mac) + mouse wheel, zooms around the pointer. The plain mouse wheel scrolls the page, not the drawing. The view stays on the storey: it cannot be zoomed out to nothing or dragged off the page (Reset view brings back the whole storey). Zoom and pan change only the view, never the drawing or a symbol's position.

reset.label: Reset view
reset.text: Shows the whole storey again. Layer ticks are not changed.

all-on.label: All layers on
all-on.text: Ticks every drawing layer of this storey, including those that are off in the DXF.

all-off.label: All layers off
all-off.text: Unticks every drawing layer, so you can then tick only the layers you want under the symbols.

filter.label: Filter layers
filter.text: Type part of a layer or base name to shorten the layer list. It only filters the list; it does not show or hide layers in the drawing.

collapse.label: Layers panel (fold)
collapse.text: Click the panel title to fold the layer panel away. The browser remembers your choice when it can (it still works when it cannot).

print.label: Print view
print.text: Switches to a print layout of this storey on one A3 landscape page: the drawing with the layers you ticked (dark on white), the electrical layers that are on, a title row, a scale note and a legend of the symbols placed. Leave it with Exit print view.

fit.label: Fit storey / Current view
fit.text: In the print view: Fit storey prints the whole storey; Current view prints the window you zoomed and panned to before opening the print view.

exit-print.label: Exit print view
exit-print.text: Returns to the editor with your layers, zoom and pan as they were.

print.note: paper_mm, margin_mm: the @page rule of the print stylesheet (generated from these values). title_mm and legend_mm: the heights of the title row and the legend on the printed page; the drawing gets the rest, which is what the scale note is computed from.
steps: Tick the drawing layers and electrical layers you want on paper.
Zoom and pan to the part you want, if you want only a part.
Click Print view. Choose Fit storey (the whole storey) or Current view (the window you zoomed to).
Press ⌘P (Mac) or Ctrl+P (Windows), or click Print / Save as PDF.
Destination: Save as PDF. Paper size: A3. Layout: landscape. Margins: none. Background graphics: on.
Click Save. Then click Exit print view to return to the editor.
print.scale_text: The scale note gives the printed scale on A3: the plan's page scale (1:100 for the sample) changed by fitting the storey or your current view to the A3 sheet.
print.browsers: Tested in Google Chrome. Safari and Firefox should work the same; check the preview before saving.

page.label: The electrical editor
page.text: One tab per storey of the plan. Drag symbols from the palette onto the drawing (or click a symbol, then click the drawing). While you place a symbol, faint rings show where the placement rules suggest it (switches beside the doors, sockets in the middle of the walls, ceiling lights in the room centre, kitchen outlets along a kitchen's walls); let go near one and the symbol snaps onto it. Move, rotate, delete and undo as needed. Connect: click a switch, then the lights it works; the page groups the lights and proposes the switch type (Ausschaltung, Wechselschaltung, Kreuzschaltung), which Apply puts in. Layout hints list lights without a switch, switches without a light and doors without a switch. Keep your work as a layout file (Save or Copy layout); Open layout brings it back.

plan.label: Open plan
plan.text: Opens a plan file (<name>.plan.json) that tools/export_plan.py wrote from your DXF. It is read in this browser and never uploaded. It is checked first, with three outcomes: a valid plan file (opened: the storeys replace the sample); another kind of file, e.g. a layout or parameter file (refused, saying what it is); or it could not be told (not JSON, not a valid plan file, a drawing that does not parse: refused, with the reason). You can also paste the file's text anywhere on the page.

paste.label: Paste a file
paste.text: Paste (⌘V / Ctrl+V) the text of a plan file, a layout file or a parameter file anywhere on the page outside an input box: the page sees which kind it is and opens it as if you had opened the file, with the same checks and the same three outcomes. Text that is not one of these is refused with the reason.

storeys.label: Storeys
storeys.text: Each storey of the plan has its own tab, its own symbols and its own draft. The sample flat has one storey.

layers.label: Drawing layers
layers.text: The plan's drawing layers of this storey, grouped by base name, with toggles per status (Bestand, Abbruch, Neubau), per base name and per layer. On screen the drawing is shown light on a black stage (each CAD colour keeps its hue, so Bestand, Abbruch and Neubau stay apart); the print is dark on white paper. Which layers are shown is saved in the layout file and applied again when it is opened.

el_layers.label: Electrical layers
el_layers.text: Placed symbols live in their own layers, one per category (Elektro – Licht, Elektro – Schalter, ...); the links (Wirkungslinien) have their own layer, Elektro – Verbindungen. Tick or untick a layer to show or hide it on screen and in the print; the numbers are the symbols (or links) on each layer.

set.label: Symbol set
set.text: Which set of symbols the palette offers. The page is built for more than one set; there is one so far. Every set says which standard it claims, its edition and where its drawings come from, and whether it was checked against the standard.

unverified.label: UNVERIFIED symbols
unverified.text: These symbols were drawn for this toolkit from general knowledge of the IEC 60617 conventions for installation plans (ÖVE/ÖNORM EN 60617; installation standard OVE E 8101). They have NOT been checked against the standard text or an Elektroplaner's legend, so a symbol may differ from the official one. Use them to plan where things go; ask the Elektroplaner to confirm the symbols before the plan is used for the installation.

palette.label: Symbol palette
palette.text: The symbols of the chosen set, grouped by category (Licht, Schalter, Steckdosen, Küche/Geräte, Daten/TV, Sicherheit, Verteiler), each with its German and English name. Drag one onto the drawing (mouse or finger), or click it (it stays selected, marked) and then click the drawing; Escape cancels. The palette folds away with its title.

place.label: Placing a symbol
place.text: Drag a symbol from the palette and let go over the drawing: its insertion point lands where you let go. Or click the symbol in the palette, then click the drawing (with the keyboard: Enter on the symbol, then Enter on the drawing places it in the middle of the view). The position is stored in drawing (model) coordinates, so zoom and pan do not move it, and it is the same position a DXF export will use.

select.label: Select and move
select.text: Click a placed symbol to select it (dashed box); drag it to move it. Click the empty drawing to deselect. Dragging the empty drawing pans the view.

rotate.label: Rotate 90°
rotate.text: Turns the selected symbol by 90 degrees counter-clockwise about its insertion point (key R). A socket's stem points to the wall it sits on: rotate until it does.

delete.label: Delete
delete.text: Deletes the selected symbol, with its links, or the selected link (keys Delete or Backspace). Undo brings it back.

undo.label: Undo / Redo
undo.text: Undo takes back the last change to the symbols and links (place, move, rotate, delete, connect, apply a proposal, open); Redo does it again (Ctrl/⌘ + Z, Ctrl/⌘ + Shift + Z). The history is kept until the page is closed.

rooms.label: Room of a symbol
rooms.text: Each placed symbol is given the id of the room it stands in, from the plan file's rooms: inside a room's outline; else the nearest label of a room that has no outline, when it is close enough (room_label_max_m in the parameters); else could-not-tell. The room is shown when the symbol is selected and saved in the layout file.

save.label: Save layout
save.text: Downloads the layout of this storey as a file <drawing>__<storey>.electrical.json (into your Downloads folder, or where the browser asks). It holds the drawing's checksum and storey, the symbol set, the shown drawing layers and every symbol with its drawing coordinates, rotation and room, and the links. Nothing leaves your computer.

save_in_place.label: Save to file (Chrome)
save_in_place.text: Shown only in browsers that can write to a file you chose (Chrome, Edge): the first click asks where to save; after that, or after Open layout in such a browser, each click saves back into the same file in place.

copy_layout.label: Copy layout
copy_layout.text: Copies the layout of this storey (the same JSON text Save layout writes) to the clipboard, so you can paste it into a file, a message or another copy of this page. When the browser does not allow the clipboard, the text is shown in a box, selected, to copy by hand.

open.label: Open layout
open.text: Opens a layout file saved or copied before (or paste its text). It is checked first, with three outcomes: it belongs to this drawing and storey (opened); it belongs to another drawing or another storey (refused, with the reason); or it could not be told (not a layout file, a damaged file, an unknown symbol set, code or rule set, or a link the symbols do not allow: refused, with the reason). Opening replaces the symbols on this tab; you are asked first when there are some, and Undo brings them back.

autosave.label: Draft in this browser
autosave.text: Every change is also kept as a draft in this browser (when it allows it; a private window may not), so closing the page by mistake loses nothing: the draft comes back when the page is opened again. The draft is not a file: save or copy the layout to keep it. Discard draft clears the tab and the draft.

file.label: Layout file format
file.text: A JSON file described by schema/el_layout.schema.json (the table below lists its fields). Positions are model (drawing) coordinates, in the drawing's units; rotation in degrees counter-clockwise; links say which switch works which light; rule_set is the placement rule set chosen. Version 2; a version-1 file still opens: it gets no links and the default rule set.

plan_file.label: Plan file format
plan_file.text: A JSON file described by schema/plan.schema.json, written by tools/export_plan.py from a DXF: per storey the drawing as SVG with one group per layer, the layer list, the model-to-drawing transform, the rooms, doors and walls with the checks R1-R5, the placement suggestions of both rule sets and, for one storey, the generated examples. It holds the DXF's file name and SHA-256, never its folder.

privacy.label: Privacy: your drawing stays on your computer
privacy.text: The page is one self-contained file: no server, no analytics, nothing loaded from other sites. A plan, layout or parameter file you open or paste is read by this browser only. Drafts stay in this browser's storage. tools/export_plan.py runs on your own computer and writes the plan file there; the plan file holds the DXF's file name and checksum, not its folder.

print.label: Print the electrical plan
print.text: Print view on a storey's tab prints the drawing layers and the electrical layers that are ticked, on one A3 landscape page with a title row, a scale note and a legend of the symbols actually placed (German names), with the note that the symbols are unverified. Then ⌘P / Ctrl+P, Save as PDF. Only in the GitHub Pages version: the shareable demo cannot print.

symbols.label: Symbols of the set
symbols.text: Every symbol of the set, with its code, names, category, target layer and the symbols it may be connected to (switch to light). Each is drawn by us, at its size in mm on the storey sheet, insertion point in the middle (+y is the wall side).

connect.label: Connect (switch to light)
connect.text: Turns Connect mode on or off. In Connect mode the switches and push-buttons are marked and everything else is dimmed. Click a switch: the symbols it may control (its 'may be connected to' list in the symbol set) are marked green and the rest stay dimmed. Then click each light it works: every click adds a link, drawn as a dashed line (Wirkungslinie) on the layer Elektro – Verbindungen. A click on a symbol the switch may not control is refused and the message names what it may control. Click another switch to start from it, the same switch again or Escape to stop. Symbols do not move in Connect mode.

links_layer.label: Links (Elektro – Verbindungen)
links_layer.text: The links between switches and lights, as dashed lines between the symbols' insertion points, on their own layer: tick it off to hide them on screen and in the print. Click a line to select it (it gets thicker); Delete removes it, Undo brings it back. Deleting a symbol deletes its links too.

groups.label: Switching groups and the proposed switch type
groups.text: A group is a set of lights that share switches (joined by links). For each group the page proposes the switch type from the number of switches: one: Ausschaltung (one-way switch); two: Wechselschaltung (two two-way switches); three or more: Kreuzschaltung (two two-way switches and an intermediate switch for every further place). A group with a push-button gets no proposal (Tasterschaltung: the Elektroplaner decides). The proposal is only shown; nothing changes until you click Apply.

apply.label: Apply the proposal
apply.text: Swaps the placed switch symbols of this group to the proposed codes (e.g. two one-way switches become two two-way switches); positions, rooms and links stay. One click, one Undo step.

rules_select.label: Placement rule set
rules_select.text: Which values the placement suggestions and the door hint use: 'starting values (to confirm)' (the default: our values, each marked 'starting value – confirm' with where its idea comes from) or 'Elektroplaner values' (empty until the Elektroplaner provides them: every rule then says 'no value yet' and gives no suggestion). The choice is saved in the layout file.

snap.label: Snap to suggestions
snap.text: When on (the default), a symbol let go near a suggestion of its kind (within the snap radius, snap_radius_m in the parameters) is placed exactly on it and turned to its wall. Switch it off, or hold Alt/Option while letting go, to place a symbol exactly where you let go.

suggestions.label: Placement suggestions (faint rings)
suggestions.text: While a symbol is being placed (dragged from the palette, picked in the palette, or moved), rings show where the chosen rule set suggests that kind of symbol on this storey; those of the room under the pointer are brighter and the one it would snap to is yellow. The rings keep their size on screen at every zoom. Tick Suggestions in the bar to see every suggestion at any time, coloured by symbol category. Hover a ring for its rule. Switches: beside each door of a room, on the room's side, on the handle side (opposite the hinge, from the door swing in the plan). Sockets: the middle of each wall piece between the doors of a room. Ceiling lights: the room centre. Kitchen and appliance outlets: along the walls of rooms whose label marks a kitchen. A room without an outline has no walls here (no socket or kitchen suggestion), a door whose swing could not be determined has no switch suggestion; the status line says how many. Windows are not known to the plan: a suggestion may fall in a window niche. Wall lights and the other symbols have no rule.

sug_all.label: Suggestions (show all)
sug_all.text: Shows every placement suggestion of the chosen rule set on this storey, coloured like the symbols it is for. Untick to hide. While you place a symbol only its own kind is shown.

rules.label: Placement rules and their values
rules.text: Every rule the suggestions and hints use, with its value in each rule set (presets/el_parameters.json, the one home for these values). A starting value is marked 'starting value – confirm' and says where the idea comes from; none is taken from a standard it was checked against.

colours.label: Colours and line widths
colours.text: On screen the stage is black in both page themes: the drawing is shown light on black and the symbols, links and rings have saturated colours. Lines keep a fixed width in screen pixels at every zoom. The print view and the printed page use white paper, the drawing dark and muted, the symbols in dark print colours and their mm widths. All colours and widths are in presets/el_parameters.json; every symbol colour has at least 3:1 contrast against its background.

hints.label: Layout hints
hints.text: A short list per storey, updated with every change, each with three outcomes (ok, to look at, could not tell). They are hints for the plan, not a check of the installation.

hint_h1.label: H1 Lights with no switch
hint_h1.text: Every light that no link reaches. Could not tell when no light is placed (nothing to check).

hint_h2.label: H2 Switches with no light
hint_h2.text: Every switch or push-button without a link. Could not tell when no switch is placed.

hint_h3.label: H3 Doors without a switch
hint_h3.text: For every room with a light: each door of the room must have a switch or push-button within the rule's distance of its opening (hint_switch_near_door_m). Could not tell: no value yet in the chosen rule set, a light whose room could not be told, a room with no door known, or a plan without rooms and doors.

params.label: Parameters (one file)
params.text: Every value you can tune is in one file, presets/el_parameters.json: the placement rules and their values in both rule sets, the snap radius, the symbol size, the room distance, the screen and print colours and the line widths, the symbols of the examples. The Parameters panel (folded at the top of the editor) shows them grouped, each with its mark ('starting value – confirm') and where it comes from (hover its name), and lets you change them: colours, widths, snap radius, symbol size, room distance and the door hint's distance apply at once; the suggestion geometry and the examples are computed when the plan file is exported, so those values apply after the plan is exported again with the changed file. Load parameters checks a file first (three outcomes). Reset brings back the page's own file. Edits are kept in this browser until Reset. Every saved layout records the parameters it was made with (id, version, SHA-256, edited or not).

params_save.label: Save parameters
params_save.text: Downloads the parameters as el_parameters.json (with the time and page it was saved from). To use them for the suggestions, put the file at presets/el_parameters.json and export the plan again. Save to file… (Chrome, Edge) writes back into a file you chose. Only in the GitHub Pages version.

params_copy.label: Copy parameters
params_copy.text: Copies the parameters (the same JSON text Save parameters writes) to the clipboard; when the browser does not allow it, the text is shown in a box, selected, to copy by hand.

params_load.label: Load parameters
params_load.text: Opens a parameter file (or paste its text) after checking it against schema/el_parameters.schema.json and the page's rules: loaded (valid, same parameters); refused as different (another page's parameters, or other sections or rules); refused as could not tell (not JSON, not a valid parameter file, or values that break the rules, e.g. a colour with less than 3:1 contrast against its background).

params_reset.label: Reset parameters
params_reset.text: Throws away your edits and loaded values and goes back to the parameters the page was built with.

example.label: Examples (simple, complex)
example.text: When you have no layout of your own on a storey, the storey chosen by the example rule opens with the SIMPLE example: one room with a ceiling light at the room centre, a two-way switch at each of its two doors (Wechselschaltung), both linked to the light, and two sockets in the middle of walls. Switch the selector to COMPLEX for the whole storey: a light, a smoke alarm and a switch at every door of each room (switch type as proposed), sockets on every wall piece, kitchen outlets in kitchens and one distribution board. Both are generated by vpt/el_examples.py from the rooms and doors of the plan and the placement suggestions (nothing is placed by hand); the symbols they use are parameters. An example is marked EXAMPLE and is never kept as a draft. As soon as you change anything it becomes your own layout (kept as a draft). Switching to another example when you have your own symbols asks first; Undo brings them back. The rule for the example's storey and room:

example_clear.label: Clear example
example_clear.text: Removes the example from this storey (symbols and links), so you start from an empty storey. Your own layouts are never touched by it.

variants.label: Two versions of this page
variants.text: The same code builds two pages (tools/build_editor.py). The GitHub Pages version is for real work: Save layout, Save to file (Chrome, Edge), Save parameters and Print view. The shareable demo (a claude.ai artifact) cannot download, save or print: there you Copy the layout or the parameters, and the draft stays in the browser. Both open a plan, layout or parameter file from your computer, or accept its text by paste.

messages.outside: Let go outside the drawing: nothing placed.
messages.armed: {name} selected: click the drawing to place it (Escape cancels).
messages.refused_unknown: Refused (could not tell whether it belongs here): {msg}.
messages.replace_confirm: Replace the {n} symbol(s) on this tab with the file's? (Undo brings them back.)
messages.copied_layout: Layout copied to the clipboard ({n} symbol(s), {l} link(s)).
messages.copy_fallback: The browser did not allow the clipboard: the text is in the box below, selected. Copy it with ⌘C / Ctrl+C.
messages.draft_restored: Your unsaved draft of this storey was restored from this browser ({n} symbol(s)).
messages.draft_discarded: Draft discarded: this tab is empty.
messages.discard_confirm: Discard the draft and every symbol on this tab?
messages.missing_layers: {n} layer(s) of the file are not in this storey and were left out.
messages.legend_note: UNVERIFIED symbols: not yet checked against ÖVE/ÖNORM EN 60617 or an Elektroplaner's legend.
messages.connect_on: Connect: click a switch (marked), then click each light it controls. Escape stops.
messages.connect_from: {name} ({code}) picked: click the lights it may control (marked): {allowed}. Others are dimmed.
messages.connect_not_switch: {code} is not a switch or push-button: in Connect mode start with a switch.
messages.ghosts: {n} suggestion(s) for {kind} (rule set: {set}); let go near one to snap (Alt/Option: place freely).
messages.no_rule: No placement rule for {name}: place it freely.
messages.no_links: No links yet: click Connect, then a switch and its light(s).
messages.link_not_allowed: Not connected: {name} ({code}) cannot be worked by {sw}. It may control: {allowed}.
messages.sug_all: Showing all {n} suggestions ({set}): colour = symbol category. Untick Suggestions to hide.
messages.params_changed: Parameter changed (kept in this browser; save or copy the parameters to keep them as a file).
messages.params_reset: Parameters reset to the page's own file.
messages.params_draft: Your edited parameters were restored from this browser (Reset brings back the page's own file).
messages.example_banner_synthetic: EXAMPLE — synthetic flat, not real data.
messages.example_default: Showing the example ({label}): change anything to make it your own, or Clear example.
messages.example_cleared: Example cleared: this storey is empty.
messages.example_replace_confirm: Replace your {n} symbol(s) on this storey with the example? (Undo brings them back.)
messages.paste_unknown: Pasted text refused (could not tell what it is): {msg}.
messages.no_storey: This plan has no storey to show.
messages.empty_storey: No symbols yet: drag one from the palette onto the drawing.

howto.label: How to use the editor
howto.intro: Each part below is one task, step by step. The words in bold are the buttons and boxes on the page; their own sections (linked at the end of each part) explain every detail.

parts.label: 0. Start from the example
steps: With no layout of your own, the example storey opens with the **simple example**, marked **EXAMPLE**.
Pick **complex** in **Example** to see a whole storey; **Clear example** empties the storey.
**Change anything** and the example becomes your own layout; switching examples then asks first.

parts.label: 1. Open your own plan
steps: On your computer, run **python3 tools/export_plan.py your.dxf**: it writes **your.plan.json** next to it.
Click **Open plan…** and pick that file (or paste its text): it is read in this browser only.
Each storey gets a tab; tick the **drawing layers** you want under the symbols.

parts.label: 2. Place symbols
steps: **Drag** a symbol from the **Symbols** palette onto the drawing and let go where it belongs, or **click** it in the palette and then **click** the drawing.
Its insertion point lands exactly where you let go; zoom and pan never move it.
**Escape** cancels a symbol picked in the palette.

parts.label: 3. Move, rotate, delete, undo
steps: **Click** a placed symbol to select it (dashed box); **drag** it to move it.
**Rotate 90°** (key **R**) turns it; a socket's stem points to its wall.
**Delete** (or the Delete key) removes the symbol or the selected link; **Undo** / **Redo** (Ctrl/⌘ + Z) take any change back.

parts.label: 4. Connect switches to lights
steps: Click **Connect**: the switches are marked; everything else is dimmed.
**Click a switch**: the symbols it may control are marked **green**; the rest stay dimmed.
**Click each light** it works: a **dashed line** (Wirkungslinie) is drawn on the layer Elektro – Verbindungen.
**Escape** or **Connect** again stops.

parts.label: 5. Switch type: proposal and Apply
steps: Under the drawing, **Switching groups** lists each set of lights that share switches.
The page **proposes** the switch type from the number of switches: 1 Ausschaltung, 2 Wechselschaltung, 3 or more Kreuzschaltung.
**Apply** swaps the placed switch symbols to the proposal; nothing changes without it.

parts.label: 6. Suggestions and snapping
steps: While you **drag or place** a symbol, **rings** show where the rules suggest that kind of symbol.
The ring it will snap to turns **yellow**; let go near it and the symbol lands exactly on it, turned to its wall.
Untick **Snap**, or hold **Alt/Option** while letting go, to place freely. Tick **Suggestions** to see every ring.

parts.label: 7. Rule sets and hints
steps: **Rules** chooses the values the suggestions use: starting values (to confirm) or the Elektroplaner's (empty until given).
**Layout hints** under the drawing list lights without a switch, switches without a light and doors without a switch nearby.

parts.label: 8. Keep your work
steps_pages: **Save layout** downloads the plan of this storey as a file; in Chrome **Save to file…** saves back into the same file.
**Open layout…** opens a saved file after checking it belongs to this drawing and storey.
A **draft** is kept in this browser after every change; **Discard draft** clears it.
steps_artifact: **Copy layout** puts the layout's text on the clipboard: paste it into a file to keep it.
**Open layout…** (or paste) opens it again after checking it belongs to this drawing and storey.
A **draft** is kept in this browser after every change; to save files, use the GitHub Pages version.

parts.label: 9. Print
steps_pages: Click **Print view** on the storey's tab: white paper, the ticked layers, print colours and a legend of the symbols placed.
Press **⌘P / Ctrl+P**, choose **Save as PDF**, A3 landscape, margins none, background graphics on.
steps_artifact: Printing is not available in this demo: open the **GitHub Pages version**, open the same plan and layout there, then **Print view**.

parts.label: 10. Parameters: change, keep, load
steps: Open **Parameters** at the top of the editor: every value, grouped; hover a name for its mark and source.
Change a value: colours, widths, snap radius, symbol size and the door hint apply **at once**; the suggestion geometry applies after the plan is **exported again**.
**Copy** (or Save) the parameters to keep them; **Load parameters…** checks a file first; **Reset** goes back to the page's own file.

entries.title: The editor in the toolkit
items: **Open plan**: your own drawing, exported on your computer by tools/export_plan.py.
**Two versions**: GitHub Pages (save, print) and a shareable demo (copy, paste).
**Synthetic sample flat** with the simple example (Wechselschaltung in the Wohnzimmer).
**Paste** a plan, layout or parameter file anywhere on the page.
**Light and dark page theme**; the drawing stage stays black.

control.in: **Around the pointer**: pinch, or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel.
control.out: **Around the pointer**: pinch, or Ctrl/⌘ + wheel.
control.pan: **Drag** the empty drawing to move it.
**Pinch** or **Ctrl/⌘ + wheel** zooms at the pointer.
**Plain wheel** scrolls the page, not the drawing.
**Reset view** brings back the whole storey.
control.reset: Layer ticks stay as they are.
control.all-on: **Ticks every drawing layer**, also those off in the DXF.
control.all-off: **Unticks every drawing layer**; then tick only what you want.
control.filter: **Type part of a name** to shorten the layer list.
Only the list: the drawing is not changed.
control.collapse: **Click the title** to fold the panel away.
Your choice is **remembered** when the browser allows.
control.print: **Tick** the layers you want; zoom if you want a part.
**Print view** → Fit storey or Current view.
control.fit: **Current view**: the window you zoomed to.
control.exit-print: **Back to the editor**, layers and zoom as before.
electrical.page: **Connect**: click a switch, then its lights.
**Save or copy** the layout to keep it.
**Example** shown until you start your own.
electrical.howto: **Step by step**: open, place, connect, keep, print.
electrical.whatsnew: **Paste** any of the three file kinds.
electrical.plan: **Read in this browser** only: nothing is uploaded.
**Checked first**: opened, or refused with why.
electrical.paste: **Paste** a plan, layout or parameter file's text.
Opened with the **same checks** as a file.
electrical.storeys: **One tab per storey**, each with its own symbols.
electrical.layers: **Drawing layers** by status, base name and layer.
Shown **light on black**; printed dark on white.
electrical.el_layers: **One layer per category**, plus the links layer.
**Untick** to hide on screen and in print.
electrical.unverified: **Drawn by us**, not checked against the standard.
**Ask the Elektroplaner** to confirm before use.
electrical.palette: **Or click it**, then click the drawing.
electrical.place: **Let go** where it belongs: the insertion point lands there.
**Near a suggestion**: it snaps onto it.
Stored in **drawing coordinates**: zoom never moves it.
electrical.select: **Click** a symbol to select it; **drag** to move it.
electrical.rotate: A socket's stem points **to its wall**.
electrical.delete: **Deletes** the selected symbol (with its links) or link.
electrical.undo: **Undo / Redo** every change: place, move, connect, apply.
electrical.rooms: **Each symbol gets its room** from the plan.
**Inside an outline**, else the nearest label, else could not tell.
electrical.save: Holds symbols, links, rule set, checksum.
electrical.save_in_place: **Chrome / Edge**: saves back into the same file.
electrical.copy_layout: **Copies the layout's text** to the clipboard.
**No clipboard**: the text is shown, selected.
electrical.open: **Opens a layout** (file or paste), checked first.
**Other drawing or storey, or unreadable**: refused, with why.
electrical.autosave: **Draft kept** in this browser after every change.
**Not a file**: save or copy the layout.
electrical.file: **Positions** in drawing coordinates; links; rule set.
electrical.privacy: **One self-contained page**: nothing loaded from elsewhere.
**Your files** are read in this browser only.
electrical.print: **Print view**: ticked drawing and electrical layers.
**White paper**, print colours, legend of placed symbols.
electrical.symbols: **Every symbol** of the set: code, names, layer.
electrical.connect: **Click a switch**: the lights it may control turn green.
**Click each light**: a dashed link is drawn.
electrical.links_layer: **Click a line** to select; **Delete** removes it.
electrical.apply: **Swaps this group's switch symbols** to the proposal.
Positions and links stay; **one Undo** step.
electrical.snap: **On**: let go near a suggestion → lands on it.
**Off**, or hold **Alt/Option**: lands where you let go.
electrical.suggestions: **Rings** show where the rules suggest a symbol.
Shown while you **place or move** a symbol.
electrical.sug_all: **Shows every suggestion** of the rule set.
**Colour** = the symbol category it is for.
electrical.rules: **Every rule and its value** in both rule sets.
**Starting value – confirm**: not from a standard.
electrical.colours: **Screen**: black stage, bright symbols, fixed-width lines.
**Print**: white paper, dark drawing, print colours.
electrical.hint_h3: **Doors of lit rooms** without a switch nearby.
electrical.params: **Hover a name**: its mark and source.
electrical.params_save: **Export the plan again** with it for the suggestions.
electrical.params_copy: **Copies the parameters' text** to the clipboard.
electrical.params_load: **Checks the file** first: loaded or refused.
**Refused**: another page's, invalid, or poor contrast.
electrical.example: **Simple**: one room, two-way switching, two sockets.
**Generated** from the rooms, doors and suggestions.
**Change anything**: it becomes your own layout.
electrical.example_clear: **Removes the example**: start from an empty storey.
electrical.variants: **Pages version**: save, save to file, print.
electrical.layer: **Tick** to show it under the symbols.
